draft.title: Depreciation
card: Depreciation is the fall in an item's value over time. Here the item loses a fixed percentage of its value each year.
The value is multiplied by the same factor each year. For 15% depreciation the factor is 0.85. This is exponential decay, like y = aˣ with a between 0 and 1.
V = V₀ × (1 − r)ⁿ. V is the value after n years, V₀ is the starting value and r is the yearly rate as a decimal.
Example: a $20 000 machine loses 10% a year for 3 years. V = 20 000 × 0.9³ = 20 000 × 0.729 = $14 580.
draft.remember: Multiply by (1 − r) once for each year. The value falls, but the rate stays the same.

a.q: A ute is bought for $50 000 and its value drops by 10% each year. What is it worth after 2 years?
a.why: V = 50 000 × 0.9² = 50 000 × 0.81 = $40 500. The value $40 000 comes from taking 10% of $50 000 off each year, which ignores that each year's loss is taken from the smaller current value.

b.q: Priya's laptop cost $2000 and loses 20% of its value each year. What is its value after 3 years?
b.why: V = 2000 × 0.8³ = 2000 × 0.512 = $1024. The value $800 comes from taking 20% of the original price off each year, which ignores that each year's loss is taken from the smaller current value.
b.clue: The factor each year is 1 − 0.20, used three times.
